meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Ortiz (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Horizon AI Head of ML), Marco Sanz (Horizon SRE), Priya Nair (Horizon Product)
summary: POC scoping focused on latency SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), p95/p99 targets, workload sizing and measurement plan. Customer wants clear pass/fail criteria and reproducible benchmark harness. Discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, KV cache/prefix caching impacts, batching, and observability needed for SLO measurement.
topics: TTFT (time to first token) vs TPOT (time per token)
p95/p99 latency targets and tail latency behavior
workload sizing: qps, avg seq len, concurrency
security and compliance checkpoints (SOC2, VPC, KMS)
timeline and next steps for 2-week POC
transcript:
00:00:00 - Samantha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Samantha, AE on the account, joined by Arjun our SE.
00:00:10 - Lena (Horizon): Hi all, Lena here. thanks for setting this up. we wanna get clear SLOs so we can measure success for the POC.
00:00:22 - Marco (Horizon SRE): Marco - we'll be running the benchmark and want to know what data you need.
00:00:30 - Samantha: Great. agenda: confirm success criteria, define TTFT vs TPOT targets (p95/p99), agree workload sizing and measurement plan, and timelines.
00:00:45 - Arjun (Redwood SE): Quick note, sometimes transcripts flip our product names - if you see Redwood Dedicated / Private confusion, we're talking about dedicated reserved GPU capacity vs private VPC install.
00:01:05 - Priya (Product): Quick question - from a product perspective, our priority is responsiveness in the UI; users complain about first-token lag more than sustained throughput.
00:01:20 - Samantha: That's helpful; that suggests TTFT may be primary for your success criteria. but we'll propose both TTFT and TPOT thresholds so you have full picture.
00:01:45 - Arjun: let's define terms so we're aligned. TTFT = time from request to first generated token returned. TPOT = average time per token after the first token, often expressed as tokens/sec or ms/token. TTFT is highly affected by model cold-start, KV cache hit-rate, and routing; TPOT correlates with batch size and hardware throughput.
00:02:20 - Marco: can you give example targets? we were thinking p95 under 250ms for first token, p99 under 400ms, and sustained throughput of roughly 2k tokens/sec would be fine for our expected load.
00:02:38 - Arjun: those are reasonable starting points. for our recommended POC we typically try to show: TTFT p95 <= 200-300ms, TTFT p99 <= 400-600ms depending on model and sequence length; TPOT expressed as tokens/sec varies widely - e.g., a quantized 7B on NVIDIA A10G might do ~500-1500 tokens/sec per GPU depending on batch/seq.
00:03:10 - Lena: our average prompt+response length is around 160 tokens; peak concurrent requests likely about 120 RPS during busy periods, average 40 RPS. does that map to TPOT numbers?
00:03:25 - Arjun: yes. quick back-of-envelope: 120 RPS * 160 tokens = 19,200 tokens/sec aggregate peak. with a per-GPU capacity of 2k-4k tokens/sec you'd need ~5-10 GPUs depending on batching and quantization. but we should run a synthetic harness with your prompt distribution to get exact numbers.
00:03:58 - Samantha: also important is the distinction between hosted/shared versus Dedicated - Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, which helps hit p99. Hosted is cheaper but tail latency can increase under noisy neighbors.
00:04:20 - Marco: We likely prefer Dedicated for the POC to get reproducible numbers. can Redwood reserve a capacity window?
00:04:27 - Samantha: yes, we can reserve a Dedicated pool for the 2-week POC window; we'll include the cost in the SOW.
00:04:40 - Priya: measurement plan - we need to be able to reproduce runs. what observability do you provide?
00:04:49 - Arjun: we'll provide a benchmark harness (scripted workload) plus dashboards. specifically: per-request metrics (TTFT, TPOT, token counts), per-model metrics, per-route breakdown, and percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and traces to pull KV-cache hit rates. We'll also export raw traces for your SRE team to ingest.
00:05:10 - Lena: excellent. can you clarify how you measure TTFT when streaming is enabled?
00:05:18 - Arjun: good question. streaming TTFT is measured when the first partial chunk is delivered to the client. if you use structured output or tool-calls, we recommend measuring the first non-empty chunk relevant to the UI. we can also measure end-to-end completion latency.
00:05:36 - Marco: about KV cache and prefix caching - our workload has many repeated prefixes; can caching materially reduce TTFT?
00:05:45 - Arjun: yes, high prefix reuse can drop TTFT significantly. our platform does prefix/KV caching; in the benchmark we can run both cold and warm cache scenarios to quantify benefit. warm cache runs will show lower TTFT and higher effective TPOT because KV hits avoid recomputation.
00:06:05 - Samantha: for pass/fail criteria, propose the POC requires two things: (1) TTFT p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 450ms on warm-cache runs for the representative prompt set; and (2) sustained aggregate TPOT capacity to meet peak tokens/sec within a 20% margin of the expected load. Thoughts?
00:06:28 - Lena: sounds reasonable but p99 450ms is tight; what about an initial ramp where we accept p99 600ms then tighten post-optim?
00:06:36 - Arjun: we can do a two-stage acceptance: baseline run target p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 600ms within week 1, and optimization run target p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 450ms by end of week 2. we'll document config changes for reproducibility.
00:06:58 - Priya: timeline wise, we need results before a potential production pilot in November. a 2-week POC starting 10/25 fits.
00:07:08 - Samantha: agreed. measurement plan details - we'll run three types of tests: cold-cache single-client latency runs, warm-cache latency runs, and throughput saturation tests (gradually increase concurrency to measure TPOT and degradation curves). each test will be repeated 3 times and we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and raw traces.
00:07:30 - Marco: what about measurement noise - should we pin runtime to Dedicated nodes and isolate network to reduce variability?
00:07:38 - Arjun: yes, Dedicated reserved GPUs remove noisy neighbors and we can put the test harness in the same VPC or region to reduce networking variance. we'll also capture system-level metrics (GPU utilization, host CPU, mem, GPU temperature) so you can correlate tail spikes.
00:07:56 - Lena: for TPOT do you report tokens/sec or ms/token? which is more actionable?
00:08:02 - Arjun: tokens/sec is easier to plan capacity, ms/token helps identify per-token compute cost. we'll report both. for SLOs it's common to specify a tokens/sec capacity target and TTFT percentiles for latency.
00:08:18 - Samantha: a quick note on quantization: models run faster when quantized, but you may see quality delta. for POC we'll run FP16/FP32 baseline then 8-bit quantized runs and include evaluation on your prompt set so you can see quality vs cost/latency tradeoff.
00:08:36 - Priya: can we include a small quality eval? like a ~200 prompt holdout set with subjective scoring?
00:08:42 - Arjun: absolutely - include that in the measurement plan. we can integrate Redwood's eval harness so you get scorecards alongside latencies.
00:08:52 - 00:12:00 - [mid-call technical dive - timestamps condensed for brevity]
00:12:05 - Marco: networking - do you recommend VPC peering or run the harness in our cloud account? we have strict egress rules.
00:12:12 - Samantha: for Dedicated POC we can either bring your harness into Redwood's reserved capacity in our cloud region with strict controls, or run the Dedicated nodes in your cloud account (Private) - latter requires more time for infra but aligns with your egress/compliance.
00:12:30 - Lena: compliance - SOC2, audit logs, encryption at rest with KMS are key. can you share security docs?
00:12:37 - Samantha: yes we'll send SOC2 and details on KMS/HSM integration. for the Private option we'll include audit log export and customer-managed keys.
00:12:50 - Priya: about reporting - can you provide a CSV of raw per-request latencies? our SRE wants that.
00:12:55 - Arjun: yes, we'll provide raw logs and dashboards. logs will include request id, start time, TTFT, tokens, TPOT, model version, cache hit boolean, and node id so you can reproduce anomalies.
00:13:12 - Marco: perfect. what about warm-up strategies before measurement? like pre-warming KV and compiling kernels?
00:13:18 - Arjun: we'll run a warm-up phase to populate caches and compile kernels. warm-up length varies - typically 5-15 minutes of representative traffic for stable kernels and KV warm state. we'll document warm-up protocol in the RUNBOOK.
00:13:35 - Lena: what about the benchmark harness itself - can we run it in our CI?
00:13:40 - Arjun: yes, the harness is a CLI with config for concurrency, prompt distribution, and streaming options. we'll hand over a Dockerized harness so it can run in your CI or our managed runner.
00:13:53 - Samantha: let's capture pass/fail and measurement artifacts: FAIL if TTFT p99 > agreed threshold after optimization window, or if sustained capacity < 80% of expected peak tokens/sec. PASS if both targets met and quality delta within agreed tolerance.
00:14:10 - Priya: what's the quality tolerance you'd propose? like BLEU or ppl is not ideal for instruction tasks; maybe subjective acceptability drop <= 7%?
00:14:20 - Arjun: propose an evaluation rubric: ask three annotators to score on helpfulness/accuracy; require average change <= 10% for quantized runs; we can tune threshold to your risk tolerance.
00:14:33 - 00:20:00 - [discussion on hardware mapping and kernel compilation specifics, intermittent crosstalk and minor transcription errors]
00:20:12 - Marco: side question - if p99 spikes, can Redwood route to fallback model to preserve availability?
00:20:18 - Samantha: yes, we support routing policies and automatic fallback to smaller/faster model variants; that affects quality but preserves SLA. we'll include fallback policies in the SOW.
00:20:35 - Lena: can you show us a sample report from a prior POC?
00:20:40 - Arjun: yes I'll share a sanitized run with TTFT/TPOT plots, p95/p99 tables, and config used - link will be in follow-up.
00:20:52 - Samantha: to recap before we open for final q's: 2-week POC starting 10/25, Dedicated reserved capacity, measurement plan includes cold/warm/throughput tests repeated 3x, pass/fail two-stage acceptance (baseline then optimization), and deliverables include raw logs, dashboard, and evaluation report.
00:21:10 - Priya: sounds good. one last item - do you support synthetic traffic that mimics multi-turn chat? our app uses multi-turn context heavily.
00:21:20 - Arjun: yes the harness supports multi-turn flows and KV cache warm scenarios; we'll parameterize conversation lengths and add sampling of prefixes.
00:21:35 - Lena: ok thanks. can you also include cost estimates for different Dedicated sizes in the SOW?
00:21:42 - Samantha: yes we'll include estimated committed GPUs and projected unit cost per 1M tokens.
00:22:00 - 00:54:00 - [call continues with clarifications on telemetry fields, SOW details, and scheduling; small sections of overlapping speech, filler words, and a few mis-transcribed proper nouns]
00:54:05 - Samantha: final quick recap of action items and owners - I'll send SOW and pricing, Arjun will share harness and baseline plots, Lena will provide prompt set and traffic profile. we'll aim to kick off 10/25.
00:54:30 - Lena: thanks everyone, looking forward.
00:54:40 - Marco: thanks.
00:54:48 - Priya: bye
00:54:55 - Samantha: bye all, talk soon.
